about: Local release conveyor belt, driven by `cargo xtask release` (xtask/src/release.rs). Each step says what to do; `done` runs its checks before moving on. {version} is replaced by the release version. Progress lives in log/release/state.json (not committed).

steps.title: Set the version
do: Make sure the work for this release is merged into main and checked out.
Set the version: `cargo xtask version set {version}` (updates Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock).

steps.title: Commit and push the version bump
do: Commit Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock: `git commit -am "Prism {version}"`.
Push main.

steps.title: Get the macOS packages from GitHub Actions
do: Release builds are never made on this Mac: the push of the version commit runs the GitHub Actions `Build` workflow (build.yml), which builds macOS Apple silicon with the embedded fonts, signs it with the Developer ID and notarizes it. Wait for it: `gh run list --repo NK-Studio/prism --workflow build.yml --limit 3` (its head must be the version commit).
Download its macOS artifact into dist/release/: `gh run download <run id> --repo NK-Studio/prism --name prism-macos-aarch64 --dir dist/release`.
A package built here (RustRover "Prism Package (macOS)", `packaging/macos/package.sh`) is ad-hoc signed and has no embedded fonts: fine for trying things, never for a release. This step refuses it.
Output: dist/release/prism-{version}-macos-aarch64.dmg and .app.zip, signed and notarized.

verify.run: spctl -a -vv -t open --context context:primary-signature dist/release/prism-{version}-macos-aarch64.dmg 2>&1 | grep -q 'source=Notarized Developer ID'

steps.title: Try the built app
do: Open dist/release/prism-{version}-macos-*.dmg (the one from GitHub Actions), drag Prism to Applications, launch it.
Help › About Prism shows {version}. Open a PSD, paint a stroke, save a copy, quit.

steps.title: Build the Windows installer
do: The same `Build` run as the macOS packages also packages Windows x64 (unsigned).

Download its Windows artifact into dist/release/: `gh run download <run id> --repo NK-Studio/prism --name prism-windows-x64 --dir dist/release` (or Actions › the run › Artifacts › prism-windows-x64, unzipped into dist/release/).
Skip this step (`cargo xtask release skip`) to ship macOS only.

steps.title: Tag the release
do: `git tag v{version}` on the version commit, then `git push origin v{version}`.

steps.title: Publish the release and the in-app update
do: RustRover: run "Prism Publish Update (dry run)" and check the printed feed and file list, then run "Prism Publish Update".
Terminal: `packaging/publish-update.sh` (add `--min-supported X.Y.Z` to send older versions to a manual download).

It signs the feed with ~/prism-update.key, uploads the .app.zip/.msi update packages and the first-install .dmg to the public GitHub Release v{version} (creating it from the tag, with packaging/release/notes.md as its notes), pushes NK-Studio/prism-updates and waits until Cloudflare serves {version}.
New users install from that release: https://github.com/NK-Studio/prism/releases/tag/v{version} (open the DMG, drag Prism onto Applications).

verify.run: gh release view v{version} --repo NK-Studio/prism --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' | grep '^prism-{version}-macos-.*[.]dmg$'

steps.title: Check the update reaches users
do: On a Mac with the previous Prism (one that has in-app updates): Help › Check for Updates… finds {version}.
Update → Restart to Update; Prism reopens and Help › About Prism shows {version}.

Skip for the first release with in-app updates: no installed copy can update yet. Also skip for the first release after 1.2.0: 1.2.0 reads the retired Vercel feed, so its users install that release by hand.
